items.w5_speech: Hi, this is Cloud from Fix-well Technology. We've finished the inspection, and I'm calling about the quotation. The total repair cost is four hundred and eighty US dollars, including parts and labor. The quotation is valid for thirty days. We'll need your confirmation in writing before we start the repair — and if you'd rather not proceed, we can return the unit as it is.

items.w5_rec1: The power module was found damaged during the electrical inspection. Quoted the replacement cost and held the unit for customer approval. The customer approved the quotation and the repair was scheduled.
items.w5_recshort1: Power module damaged @ electrical inspection → quoted replacement, held for approval → approved, repair scheduled.
items.w5_rec2: Two capacitors measured out of specification during the functional test. Listed both parts in the quotation together with the estimated labor time. The quotation was sent and acknowledged by the customer the same day.
items.w5_recshort2: 2 caps out of spec @ functional test → listed in quote w/ labor est. → quote sent, acknowledged same day.
items.w5_rec3: The board damage was beyond economical repair. Informed the customer and offered to return the unit as it is. The customer chose to have the unit returned without repair.
items.w5_recshort3: Damage beyond economical repair → informed customer, offered return as-is → returned, no repair.
items.w5dg1: How much will the repair cost?
items.w5dg2: How long is this quotation good for?
items.w5dg3: Can you just start the repair now?
items.w5dg4: What if I decide not to repair it?
items.w6_s1: I understand the cost is higher than expected — let me explain what it covers.
items.w6_s2: The quotation covers three replacement parts and about four hours of labor.
items.w6_s3: We can reduce the cost if we repair only the failing channel.
items.w6_s4: Unfortunately, we are not able to lower the price further at this stage.
items.w6_s5: Would you like us to quote the alternative option for comparison?
items.w6_speech: Hi Mr. Yeh, this is Cloud from Fix-well Technology. I understand the cost is higher than you expected — let me explain what it covers. The quotation covers three replacement parts and about four hours of labor. If you'd like to bring the cost down, we can repair only the failing channel instead of all four. Unfortunately we're not able to lower the price further at this stage, but I'm happy to quote the alternative option so you can compare.

items.w6_rec1: Only one of the four channels failed the functional test. Quoted a partial repair covering the failing channel only. The customer accepted the partial repair and the work was scheduled.
items.w6_recshort1: 1 of 4 ch failed @ functional test → quoted partial repair, failing ch only → accepted, scheduled.
items.w6_rec2: The customer questioned the labor hours listed in the quotation. Broke the labor time down into inspection, replacement, and retest. The customer accepted the breakdown and approved the original quotation.
items.w6_recshort2: Customer questioned labor hrs → broke down: inspect / replace / retest → accepted, original quote approved.
items.w6_rec3: The requested discount was below our minimum repair charge. Explained the minimum charge and offered a reduced repair scope instead. The customer selected the reduced scope and the case moved forward.
items.w6_recshort3: Requested discount < min charge → explained min charge, offered reduced scope → customer took reduced scope.
items.w6dg1: This is more than we budgeted for.
items.w6dg2: Why is the labor cost so high?
items.w6dg3: Can you give us a 30% discount?
items.w6dg5: What if we only fix the broken part?

items.w7_speech: Hi Mr. Yeh, this is Cloud from Fix-well Technology. We've issued RMA number R dash two four zero eight one for this case. Before you ship the unit back, please fill in the RMA form I attached, and mark the RMA number clearly on the outside of the package. The unit should go in its original box, or equivalent protective packaging. Once we receive it, we'll confirm by email — and if you can send me the tracking number, I'll keep an eye out for it.

items.w7_rec1: The unit arrived without an RMA number marked on the package. Matched the serial number against the open RMA list and logged the unit manually. The unit was accepted and the customer was asked to mark the number on future shipments.
items.w7_recshort1: Unit arrived, no RMA# on box → matched S/N vs open RMA list, logged manually → accepted, customer reminded.
items.w7_rec2: One corner of the package was crushed on arrival. Photographed the packaging and checked the unit for shipping damage before opening the case. No damage was found on the unit and the inspection continued as planned.
items.w7_recshort2: Box corner crushed on arrival → photographed packaging, checked for shipping damage → unit OK, inspection continued.
items.w7_rec3: The unit was shipped without any protective foam inside the box. Reported the packaging issue to the customer with photos taken at receiving. The customer agreed to use protective packaging for future shipments.
items.w7_recshort3: No protective foam in box → reported to customer w/ receiving photos → customer agreed to pack properly next time.
items.w7dg1: Do I need an RMA number before sending it?
items.w7dg2: I threw away the original box. Is that a problem?
items.w7dg3: Where exactly should I write the RMA number?
items.w7dg4: How will I know you received it?
items.w7dg5: Should I send the power cable and accessories too?

items.w8_speech: Hi Mr. Yeh, this is Cloud from Fix-well Technology. I'm calling with an update on RMA R dash two four zero eight one. The estimated completion date is August fifteenth. The replacement part has a lead time of about two weeks, and we'll start the repair as soon as it arrives. The schedule may change if the supplier delays the shipment — but if the estimated date changes, I'll update you right away.

items.w8_rec1: The replacement relay was not in stock when the repair was scheduled. Placed an order and informed the customer of the two-week lead time. The relay arrived on schedule and the repair was completed the same week.
items.w8_recshort1: Relay out of stock @ scheduling → ordered, told customer 2-wk lead time → arrived on time, repair done same week.
items.w8_rec2: The supplier delayed the power module shipment by one week. Informed the customer of the revised estimated completion date. The unit was completed one week later than originally planned.
items.w8_recshort2: Supplier delayed power module 1 wk → informed customer, revised ETA → completed 1 wk later than planned.
items.w8_rec3: The repair was finished ahead of the estimated completion date. Notified the customer and arranged an earlier shipment. The unit was returned three days ahead of schedule.
items.w8_recshort3: Repair finished ahead of ETA → notified customer, arranged earlier shipment → returned 3 days early.
items.w8dg1: When will the repair be finished?
items.w8dg2: Why does it take two weeks?
items.w8dg3: Can you start the repair before the part arrives?
items.w8dg4: What if the supplier is late again?
items.w8dg5: The unit is finished earlier than expected — great!
